boundary: Synthetic evidence only. Figures do not show observed animal movement, crossing use, collision reduction, population response, biodiversity benefit, approval, or a design-ready project.

figures.alt_text: Two stacked 20 by 12 synthetic Circuitscape current grids show the no-action baseline above the selected candidate on one color scale. Amber outlines the same 48 road-review cells. Their summed current is 1.0638 at baseline and 1.5675 for the candidate, a 47.35 percent increase.
figures.caption: The same 48-cell road-review mask is used in both direct current rasters, on a shared scale. Its summed current rises from 1.0638 to 1.5675 in this safeguard scenario, a 47.35% change. This is a circuit diagnostic, not animal-use evidence.
figures.forbidden_implication: Animal routes, animal-use probability, collision locations, or harm.
figures.question: What direct raster calculation produced the road-area review flag?
figures.takeaway: The same 48-cell current sum rises 47.35 percent; this is a circuit diagnostic.
figures.title: Baseline and candidate current

figures.alt_text: The actual EcoCorridor Evidence Rail displays a negative 1.60 percent baseline-relative resistance change and its candidate and baseline jobs, safeguard scenario, matrix SHA-256, and accepted fixture QA.
figures.caption: Opening the controlling result shows the calculation, baseline and candidate jobs, a saved matrix hash, and numerical QA. These records let a reviewer check the calculation; the ecological assumptions still require separate review.
figures.forbidden_implication: Artifact identity as proof of ecological validity.
figures.question: Can a reader reconstruct the controlling 1.6031 percent result?
figures.takeaway: The result resolves to its calculation, direct jobs, matrix hash, and numerical QA.
figures.title: Checking the controlling result

figures.alt_text: A downward flow follows authorized evidence into bounded provider and read-only tool work. Required release checks combine exact Weave trace readback, current authorization, local validation, and deterministic rendering before an unconfirmed draft is saved. Missing evidence, provider or tool failure, and failed release checks each exit to no draft.
figures.caption: Only a validated output with an exact Weave trace readback can become an unconfirmed draft. The historical agent used a fixed tool sequence; this diagram does not claim selective retrieval or autonomous review.
figures.forbidden_implication: Autonomous model changes, selective traversal, ecological judgment, or approval.
figures.question: What must succeed before the tested agent output can become a saved draft?
figures.takeaway: Authorized direct evidence, local validation, and exact Weave readback are all required.
figures.title: Preparing a review brief

figures.alt_text: Across four teaching-portfolio cases, horizontal bars show 10,798 full-context input tokens and 10,542 agent input tokens. A reduction chart places the observed 2.37 percent beside the 25 percent promotion gate. Notes identify fixed agent traversal and comparator answer hints; the deterministic checklist remains default.
figures.caption: Across the four teaching-portfolio cases, the historical agent used 256 fewer input tokens, a 2.37% reduction against a 25% gate. Fixed traversal and answer-contract hints in the full-context comparator limit the comparison. The deterministic checklist stayed default.
figures.forbidden_implication: Fair agent ranking, practitioner usefulness, or adaptive retrieval benefit.
figures.question: Did this historical agent clear the input-token reduction gate?
figures.takeaway: Its 2.37 percent reduction missed the 25 percent gate; the comparator was also confounded.
figures.title: Historical input-token comparison
